query: When does private defence of body extend to causing death?

gold_references.label: Section 38
gold_references.role: conditions under which private defence of body extends to causing death

acceptable_references.label: Section 37
acceptable_references.reason: sets restrictions on the right of private defence

required_points: Section 38 provides that the right of private defence of body extends to causing death if the assault may reasonably cause apprehension of death, apprehension of grievous hurt, assault with intent to commit rape, assault with intent to gratify unnatural lust, assault with intent to kidnap or abduct, assault with intent to wrongfully confine a person in a situation where they cannot seek public authority protection, or an act of throwing or administering acid.
optional_points: The right is subject to the restrictions specified in Section 37.
forbidden_points: Private defence of body always extends to causing death for any assault.
Death can be caused in private defence only when the attacker uses a weapon.

notes: Direct lookup. Section 38 lists specific situations. Answer must be grounded in the listed categories.
